policy: Forbidden metrics and non-dispositive diagnostics must not be used as legal correctness gates in the v1 HS legal extraction evaluation harness.

guardrails.text: Any truncation, chunk-boundary loss, context-window loss, or retrieval-window omission must be logged as a source-processing boundary.

metrics.name: Negative Log Likelihood
metrics.rationale: NLL is not implementable or auditable in typical LLM-as-a-service legal extraction contexts because token probabilities are unavailable and do not map to legal authority.

metrics.name: Brier Score
metrics.rationale: Brier scores require calibrated probability forecasts. The harness uses legal authority, source grounding, and route safety rather than probabilistic correctness.

metrics.name: TF-IDF / Entropy As Domain Relevance Proxy
metrics.rationale: Term-frequency proxies cannot distinguish legal authority, binding force, jurisdictional scope, or provenance sufficiency.

metrics.name: Document-Level Citation For Material Propositions
metrics.rationale: Document-level citation is too broad for legal auditability when finer anchors are available. Material propositions require sub-document anchors where possible.

metrics.name: BERTScore
metrics.rationale: Semantic similarity can support paraphrase diagnostics later, but it cannot validate legal authority, source sufficiency, or handoff safety.

metrics.name: Expected Calibration Error
metrics.rationale: ECE needs probability bins and empirical accuracy sets. V1 uses false-certainty and uncertainty-preservation controls instead.

metrics.name: nLog-Distance
metrics.rationale: nLog-Distance is useful for numeric threshold-heavy regulatory domains, but it is not a core HS legal extraction metric for v1.
